title: Two Sum
problem_statement: Given an array of integers and a target value, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target.
hints: Think about complements.
A hash map can reduce lookup time.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problem_statement: Given daily stock prices, compute the maximum profit possible from a single buy followed by a single sell.
hints: Track the lowest price seen so far.
Update the best profit as you scan.

title: Valid Anagram
problem_statement: Determine whether two strings are anagrams of each other.
hints: Character counts matter more than order.
Compare frequency maps or sorted forms.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problem_statement: Return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated characters.
hints: A sliding window can expand and shrink as needed.
Track the most recent index of each character.

title: Group Anagrams
problem_statement: Group words that are anagrams of each other and return the grouped lists.
hints: Use a canonical key for each word.
Sorting or character counting can produce the grouping key.

title: Container With Most Water
problem_statement: Given vertical lines on a chart, find the pair that forms the container with the maximum area.
hints: Start with the widest container.
Move the shorter wall inward first.

title: Valid Parentheses
problem_statement: Determine whether a string of brackets is balanced and properly nested.
hints: Opening brackets need to be matched later.
The latest unmatched opening bracket matters first.

title: Moving Average From Data Stream
problem_statement: Design a structure that returns the moving average of the last k values in a stream.
hints: Keep only the recent values you still need.
Track the running sum to avoid recomputing.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problem_statement: Remove the nth node from the end of a singly linked list and return the updated head.
hints: Two pointers can keep a fixed gap.
A dummy head simplifies edge cases.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problem_statement: Traverse a binary tree level by level and return the values for each depth.
hints: Think breadth-first traversal.
A queue helps process one level at a time.

title: Number of Islands
problem_statement: Count the number of islands in a 2D grid of land and water cells.
hints: Each unseen land cell starts a traversal.
Mark visited cells so you do not count the same island twice.

title: Climbing Stairs
problem_statement: Count how many distinct ways you can reach the top if you can climb one or two steps at a time.
hints: The current answer depends on the previous two states.
Build from the smallest stair counts upward.

title: Coin Change
problem_statement: Given coin denominations and a target amount, compute the fewest coins needed to make that amount.
hints: Think about the best solution for smaller amounts first.
Use a sentinel for unreachable states.

title: Subsets
problem_statement: Return all possible subsets of a list of unique integers.
hints: At each step you can choose to include or exclude the current element.
Backtracking is a natural fit.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problem_statement: Search for a target in a rotated sorted array and return its index, or -1 if missing.
hints: One half is always sorted.
Use that sorted half to decide where the target can still live.

title: Course Schedule
problem_statement: Determine whether all courses can be completed given prerequisite pairs.
hints: This is a cycle detection problem.
Topological ordering or DFS state tracking both work.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
problem_statement: Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary tree.
hints: Think recursively about what each subtree reports upward.
A subtree can tell you whether it found one or both targets.

title: LRU Cache
problem_statement: Design an LRU cache that supports O(1) get and put operations.
hints: You need both fast lookup and fast reordering.
A hashmap plus doubly linked list is the classic pairing.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problem_statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in an array.
hints: Start with a quadratic DP solution before optimizing.
Each element can extend earlier subsequences.

title: Network Delay Time
problem_statement: Given directed weighted edges, find how long it takes for a signal to reach all nodes from a starting node.
hints: You need shortest paths from one source.
A priority queue helps process the next best frontier node.
